description:
fz2 run on a program building [1 | 2] panics: fz_list_cons_int ExpectedTag (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1874). At 62c02cb1a, `dbg([1 | 2])` also fails on interp: "backend list: cannot allocate list cons: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(1), found: ValueKind(13) }". Elixir builds the improper list and inspect renders [1 | 2]. Done when: an oracle fixture building, matching and inspecting improper lists agrees on interp, run and build, and fixture 00665 gains the improper `[1] ++ 2` case it had to leave out.

Also covered here: length/1 of an improper list in a guard. The guard census for GH #303 found it is an interpreter internal error and a JIT/AOT abort; Elixir's guard fails and the next clause is tried. Since fz-rs7.4 a failed operation in a guard leaves its clause unmatched, so once an improper list can be built the oracle fixture adds: def f(l) when length(l) > 0 applied to [1 | 2] answers the next clause on interp, run and build.

Macro.escape (fz-sc8.225) meets an improper list once one exists: Elixir's Macro.escape([1 | 2]) is [{:|, [], [1, 2]}] and Macro.escape([1, 2 | 3]) is [1, {:|, [], [2, 3]}]. Done when also: lib/macro.fz's list escape writes that form, and the oracle fixture shows it.

Measured by Optimize at develop ec0ca8a8a plus fz-sc8.192.3, release fz2, 2026-11-20: `dbg([1 | 2])` under fz2 run exits 0 and prints `[1, #slot<0x2:0>]` (silent wrong output, not a panic). `it = [0 | %{a: 1}]; dbg(it)` exits 139 (SIGSEGV) under run and build; interp fails with "backend list: cannot allocate list cons: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(1), found: ValueKind(2) }". Done when also: the oracle fixture covers a map tail ([0 | %{a: 1}], the shape of OTP's map iterator [Path | Map], maps.erl:1060) and a scalar tail printed under run (the JIT's silent print).

Third sighting (Callables, fz-9x7.44.3 probe, 2026-11-21, develop 49e06fe93): def t(x), do: [1 | x]; l = t(2); [_ | y] = l; IO.inspect(y). Elixir prints 2. interp: 'cannot allocate list cons: ExpectedTag'. run: panic 'misaligned pointer dereference ... 0xa5a5a5a5a5a5a5' at runtime/src/any_value.rs:1160 (reads garbage memory). Typing: y + 1 is typed as ([int], int), i.e. the cons-pattern tail of [1 | x] is assumed a list (fz-sc8.22.1). The cons tail readers refuse a non-list tail at list_tail_bits_from_ref (runtime/src/heap/ref_io.rs:98) (fz-sc8.22.2). Probe: Callables' scratchpad improper/q.fz.

comments.text: fz-sc8.10 (49f85b767) deleted the renderer's improper-list branch because no list tail could be anything but a list. When [1 | 2] becomes a value, runtime/src/any_value.rs's Renderer must print it as Elixir's Inspect.Algebra.container_each does: the ... check comes first, then [left | right] renders both without charging the tail against limit (Elixir 1.19.4: inspect([1 | 2], limit: 1) = [1 | 2]; inspect([1, 2 | 3], limit: 1) = [1, ...]; inspect([1, 2 | 3]) = [1, 2 | 3]). Also: keyword? and List.ascii_printable? are false for an improper list.
OTP json.erl parity (fz-mue) needs this; reproducer from the faithful port: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-otp-json/punch/25_improper_list_stack.fz

Second reproducer (JSON, 2026-11-20): /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-otp-json/punch/mue25/u4.fz. Enum.reduce([1, 2], :start, fn x, acc -> [x | acc] end) builds the improper list [2, 1 | :start] and fails on interp with the same 'cannot allocate list cons: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(1), found: ValueKind(15) }'. Owner: Bugs and Cleanup (assigned by Coordinator).

title: An improper list is built, matched and inspected as in Elixir
